_comment: The pages whose text is built from data outside their own file, and that data.
src/lib/content-dates.mjs dates a page by the last commit that changed its content;
a page listed here is also dated by the newest commit to each of its sources, so a
count, a table or a report it renders moves its date the day it changes.
Paths are from the repository root, and one ending in / is a directory.
In "sources", every commit that changed a file counts, except that a directory of
the content tree stands for its pages, each dated by the page rule. "counts" names
each number a page shows of other files after the export that computes it, and
only a commit that changed that number moves the page. A list of git pathspecs is
a number of files, named after its src/data/repo-stats.mjs export; a pathspec that
holds {topic} stands for one per topic the navigation teaches (domainIds in
src/data/topics.mjs, the topics repo-stats.mjs counts the guides under). An object
{"file": path, "lines": pattern} is the number of lines of that file the pattern
matches, named after its src/data/conformance-stats.mjs export: an edit inside an
entry leaves it, a new entry moves it. {"report": path, "drawnBy": component} is
each page's own: the "Verified by" line under a guide's title, which the component
draws from that report and the page's references, so a commit to the report made
since the component was added moves a page only when it changed the line that page
shows; one from before then changed no line anyone saw. "texts" names each text a
page shows of other files after the export that reads it: {"files": pathspecs,
"pattern": pattern} is every match of the pattern in those files, and only a commit
that changed one moves the page. The entry whose pages are the whole content tree
answers for the layout, the components astro.config.mjs mounts on every page. The
build fails on a page or a source HEAD does not have.
site/scripts/content-dates.test.mjs fails on a page that reaches data without an
entry here, on a layout that does with no entry for the whole tree, on an entry that
leaves out a data module or a reader of the content collection its pages reach, or a
module that carries one of them into the page, on a count that is not the number its
export computes, and on a text that is not the one its export reads. Keys beginning
with an underscore are notes to the build; the test
reads "_via", which maps each module the pages reach and are not dated by to the
source or count that stands for it, or to the reason it moves no page. A reason given
for repo-stats.mjs or conformance-stats.mjs, which read the repository as the site
builds, names in backticks each export of it the pages take, and stands for those alone.

entries._why: Every page is drawn in the same layout, the components astro.config.mjs mounts in Starlight's place, and what the layout shows of other files is on every page. One thing of it is a page's own content: the line under a guide's title that says how many conformance checks verify it and in which domains of the report (src/components/VerifiedBy.astro). It is drawn from docs/conformance.json and the page's own references, so each page is dated by its own line: a commit to the report moves a page only when the line that page shows changed. How the line is drawn and named (VerifiedBy.astro, src/lib/conformance-evidence.mjs) moves no page, as the header chips' code moves none; the numbers it draws do. The rest of what the layout shows is the site's frame.

_via.site/src/lib/bibliography-works.ts: the works the bibliography page's structured data defines in full, read from every page's references, and the works an errata page's structured data says it corrects: data for machines, which no reader of a page reads
_via.site/src/data/repo-stats.mjs: `version` and `targetPlatform`, the release and the Python an API page's structured data names, data for machines, and `version` again in the BibTeX entry citation.mjs builds, which the page actions hold in an attribute to copy, the same on every page and no part of any one: no reader of a page reads either as its text
_via.site/src/lib/catalogue-pages.ts: the catalogue pages the structured data of a catalogue page and of the catalogue overview names: data for machines, which no reader of a page reads
_via.site/src/generated/catalogues.mjs: the columns the Dataset of a catalogue page says it measures: data for machines, which no reader of a page reads
_via.site/src/data/topics.mjs: the navigation the sidebar, the breadcrumbs, a topic's mark beside its title and a topic's own section list draw, which moves no page's date, as a page's sidebar entry does not
_via.site/src/generated/api-sidebar.mjs: the API groups topics.mjs builds the sidebar from: navigation, which moves no page's date
_via.site/src/lib/content-dates.mjs: the dates themselves, which read every page's references to date each one by its own line, and which the footer and the structured data print
_via.site/src/lib/page-references.mjs: the references of every page, read for the dates by the line each page shows, which counts.verifiedBy already dates each page by
the weights the head gives the designations it declares to the search index, which no reader of a page sees
_via.site/src/data/citation.mjs: the citation of the library the page actions offer to copy, the same on every page and no part of any one

entries._why: The landing page states the conformance counts, the release, the Python it needs and the line that installs it, the catalogue rows and how many guides, API pages and fiches there are. The counts are those the summary banner prints, which make conformance draws from the report and CI holds to it; the report itself also changes with every value and name in it, which the landing page does not show. repo-stats.mjs and conformance-stats.mjs compute the numbers, so every commit to them can change one the page shows: the guides went from 163 to 168 by a change to how repo-stats.mjs picks the topics it counts, with no guide added.

_via.site/src/data/topics.mjs: the icon each area row carries, matched on its link, and the topics the guides are counted under, which counts.guides takes through {topic}, so a topic added with its guides moves the page. A topic added over guides its folder already holds, or a topic that did not teach made one that does, changes the number with no guide added, and that commit moves nothing, since the count reads every commit through the topics of the tree it builds: dating the page by topics.mjs instead would move it with every edit to the navigation, a label, an order or an icon, that changes no number it shows
_via.site/src/generated/api-sidebar.mjs: the API groups topics.mjs builds the sidebar from, none of which the landing page shows

entries._why: The conformance report is the report itself, rendered, with the releases it was archived with.

_via.site/src/lib/content-dates.mjs: the dates the report reads its last commit from, which read every page's references to date each guide by its own line; the report shows none of it
_via.site/src/lib/page-references.mjs: reached through the dates on the same path, and the report shows none of it
_via.site/src/data/topics.mjs: reached through the dates the report reads its last commit from (src/lib/date-rules.mjs counts the guides under its topics), and the report shows none of it
_via.site/src/generated/api-sidebar.mjs: reached through topics.mjs on the same path, and the report shows none of it

entries._why: These guides quote the conformance counts, as the summary banner prints them and conformance-stats.mjs reads them.

This guide quotes the conformance counts and the number of errata entries, which conformance-stats.mjs counts as the second-level headings of docs/ERRATA.md. That number is all the page shows of the registry, so a commit that rewraps or corrects an entry leaves the page's date where it is, and one that adds an entry moves it.
The glossary is its data module, rendered.

_via.site/src/components/Glossary.astro: the title of each guide a term links to, printed as the link: a title moves no page's date, its own included, so a guide retitled without a change to glossary.mjs leaves the glossary's date where it is

entries._why: The index of fiches lists every fiche the repository ships, under the title and with the sentence the guide that shows it gives it in its <ReportPreview>, which reports.mjs reads off the guides: the Spanish index off the Spanish twins, with the English guides for its areas and for any fiche a twin does not declare. A commit that changes one of those declarations moves both indexes, and one that changes the rest of a guide moves neither. Each line also names the guide by its title, which moves no page's date, its own included.

Each catalogue page renders its tables from the generated catalogue data, and the finder on every page and the list on the overview name each catalogue with its rows. CatalogueFinder.astro and CatalogueIndex.astro write those words, so a commit to either moves the pages. The directory stands for every page under it, the overview included, so a commit to Catalogues.astro moves the overview and one to CatalogueIndex.astro moves the catalogue pages, though neither shows what that component writes.

_via.site/src/lib/catalogue-pages.ts: the label, description and catalogue keys of every catalogue page, which the finder and the overview list: a label or a description moves no page's date anywhere on the site, and a catalogue key arrives with its rows in catalogues.mjs, a source
_via.site/src/data/topics.mjs: the order of the catalogue pages (catalogueSlugs), which the finder and the overview follow; a catalogue joins it with its rows in catalogues.mjs, a source
_via.site/src/generated/api-sidebar.mjs: the API groups topics.mjs builds the sidebar from, none of which these pages show
